questions.question: Who among the following was the slave-general of Alauddin Khilji, who led his army in the battle against Ramachandra of Devagiri?
questions.solution:
• General: Malik Kafur
  • Sultanate: He was the first to take the Delhi Sultanate's flags deep into South India.

questions.question: The Ashtadhyayi of Panini is a renowned work on ________.
questions.solution:
• Grammar: Sanskrit Grammar
  • Panini: The Ashtadhyayi is an eight-chapter treatise that standardized the Sanskrit language.

questions.question: Malik Ambar, who resisted Mughals in Deccan, was an able administrator of which state?
questions.solution:
• State: Ahmednagar
  • Leader: Malik Ambar was a former slave who became the regent and introduced land reforms in Ahmednagar.

questions.question: The authorities of which country denied the permission to land the ship Komagata Maru, carrying Indians?
questions.solution:
• Country: Canada
  • Incident: The Komagata Maru was a Japanese steamship carrying Indian immigrants that was turned away from Vancouver.

questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act enacted in British India?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1878
  • Act: The Vernacular Press Act was introduced by Lord Lytton to suppress non-English newspapers.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Aligarh Movement, which was largely responsible for the revival of Muslims in India?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Sayyid Ahmad Khan
  • Movement: The Aligarh Movement aimed at modernizing Muslim education and reconciling it with Western science.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan kings gave up war after the battle of Kalinga?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Ashoka
  • Transformation: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka replaced Bherighosha (war drum) with Dhammaghosha (sound of peace).

questions.question: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced a copper coin called __________ in place of the silver coin.
questions.solution:
• Coinage: Jittal
  • Reform: Muhammad bin Tughlaq attempted a token currency experiment using copper/brass coins.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders led the Bardoli Satyagraha?
questions.solution:
• Leader: Vallabhbhai Patel
  • Title: His success in the Bardoli Satyagraha earned him the title 'Sardar' from the women of Bardoli.

questions.question: Who led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar?
questions.solution:
• Revolt: Veer Kunwar Singh
  • 1857: Despite his old age, Kunwar Singh was the most successful military leader of the revolt in Bihar.

questions.question: Sisodiya Rajput ruler of Mewar, Amar Singh accepted Mughal services during the reign of ________.
questions.solution:
• Mughal: Jahangir
  • History: After decades of conflict, Amar Singh of Mewar submitted to Jahangir on honorable terms.

questions.question: ________was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni in the Buddhism.
questions.solution:
• First Bhikkhuni: Mahapajapati Gotami
  • Ordination: She was the maternal aunt of Buddha and led the first female wing of the Sangha.

questions.question: Tansen, who was included in the Navaratnas of Akbar, was an expert in playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
• Instrument: Rabab
  • Tansen: He was a legendary dhrupad singer and a master of the stringed Rabab.

questions.question: Who sent the Greek ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
• Sender: Seleucus
  • Diplomacy: Seleucus Nicator sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya following a peace treaty.

questions.question: The famous scientist, Albert Einstein, was inspired by whose idea of non-violence?
questions.solution:
• Inspiration: Mahatma Gandhi
  • Physics: Albert Einstein famously said of Gandhi, 'Generations to come will scarce believe that such a one as this ever in flesh and blood walked upon this earth.'

questions.question: Diwan-i-Arz was essentially the department of ________ under Delhi Sultanate.
questions.solution:
• Department: military services
  • Sultanate: Diwan-i-Arz was the Ministry of Defense, first organized by Balban.

questions.question: The rule of the English East India company was ended in British India under the Government of India Act, __________.
questions.solution:
• Act: 1858
  • Shift: The Government of India Act 1858 transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown.

questions.question: Imadshahi family was known for the foundation of which state?
questions.solution:
• State: Berar
  • Dynasty: The Imad Shahi dynasty was one of the five Deccan Sultanates.

questions.question: Who among the following was the author of ‘Indica’, an account of India under the reign of the Maurya dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Author: Megasthenes
  • Work: Indica provides the earliest foreign account of Indian administration and society.

questions.question: Moplahs, or Muslim peasants, created a powerful anti-zamindar movement in:
questions.solution:
• Peasants: Kerala
  • Moplah: The Moplah Rebellion (1921) was a major uprising of Muslim tenants against Hindu landlords and British rule.

questions.question: Who among the following advocated the ideology of “oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu” (one caste, one religion, one god for humankind)?
questions.solution:
• Ideology: Narayana Guru
  • Social Reform: He worked against the untouchability system in Kerala and built temples open to all.

questions.question: Lord Curzon declared the partition of _________ in 1905.
questions.solution:
• Viceroy: Lord Curzon
  • Bengal: The 1905 partition was justified as administrative convenience but was actually aimed at weakening Indian nationalism.

questions.question: The origin of ‘Carnatic music’ is related to which of the following Dynasties?
questions.solution:
• Music: Vijayanagar
  • Origin: The Carnatic system was codified during this era, with Purandara Dasa known as its 'Pitamaha.'

questions.question: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade carried out their work of religious reforms in Maharashtra through which of the following organisations?
questions.solution:
• Organization: Prarthana Samaj
  • Maharashtra: This society focused on monotheism and social reforms like widow remarriage.

questions.question: ‘Hind Swaraj’ or ‘Indian Home Rule’ is written by which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.solution:
• Work: Mahatma Gandhi
  • Philosophy: Hind Swaraj (1909) outlines Gandhi's views on self-rule and his critique of modern civilization.

questions.question: “Amatya” in the Saptang Theory of Kautilya denotes which of the following?
questions.solution:
• Theory: Minister and Officials
  • Saptang: Kautilya’s Saptang Theory defines the state as having 7 limbs; Amatya is the administrative backbone.

questions.question: Abdur Razzaq, an envoy from Persia came to Vijaynagar during the reign of whose rule?
questions.solution:
• Envoy: Deva Raya II
  • Account: Abdur Razzaq visited the Hampi bazaar and described the empire's massive wealth.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in _____.
questions.solution:
• Return: January 1915
  • Gandhi: He arrived at Apollo Bunder in Bombay on 9th January, now celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.question: In 1908, _________ and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage that was occupied, they believed, by Kingsford, the unpopular judge of Muzzafarpur.
questions.solution:
• Event: Khudiram Bose
  • Revolution: The Kingsford assassination attempt led to Khudiram becoming one of the youngest martyrs of the movement.

questions.question: The capital of Vajji Mahajanapada was ______.
questions.solution:
• Capital: Vaishali
  • Republic: Vajji was a powerful Gana-Sangha (republic) made up of eight clans.
